changes.current: The course encoder creates a local fictional frame.
changes.acceptance: Accept after an exact independent byte comparison and bounded input validation.
changes.commit: Local enqueue alone is not a durable commit boundary.
changes.ack: Return only a provisional transport result until the chosen gate is met.
changes.replay_source: Replay the same accepted frames from a trusted ordered copy.
changes.failure_domain: One host holds the local queue and can lose it.

changes.current: The exercise assigns increasing sequence numbers to frames.
changes.acceptance: Reject a gap, duplicate sequence, bad epoch, or corrupt frame before mutation.
changes.commit: A sequence assignment is not itself a replicated or durable commit.
changes.ack: Reply with the original cached result after a committed request is applied.
changes.replay_source: Reconstruct state from a known prefix and its ordered suffix.
changes.failure_domain: A single writer and journal on one host share host loss.

changes.current: The course has no durable journal implementation.
changes.acceptance: Propose admitting only framed requests whose bytes are fully validated.
changes.commit: Propose a recorded and synced prefix before durable acknowledgement.
changes.ack: Acknowledge after the specified durable gate and application result.
changes.replay_source: Read the committed prefix from verified journal files.
changes.failure_domain: Define whether journal copies occupy separate hosts and disks.

changes.current: The release function is a local model, not an election protocol.
changes.acceptance: Fence a writer whose epoch differs from the active epoch.
changes.commit: Name the exact durable release condition.
changes.ack: Reconcile uncertain requests by their stable origin and request ID.
changes.replay_source: Start at the committed prefix and restore cached results.
changes.failure_domain: Two processes on one laptop share a failure domain.

changes.current: The exercise has no snapshot writer or recovery service.
changes.acceptance: Capture a consistent state at a named applied sequence.
changes.commit: Keep the checkpoint and suffix under one documented recovery policy.
changes.ack: Preserve original request results across a restore and retry.
changes.replay_source: Restore the checkpoint then apply an exact ordered suffix.
changes.failure_domain: Checkpoint and log placement determine joint-loss risk.

changes.current: The course measures a supplied list of latency samples.
changes.acceptance: Count each accepted and delivered message before interpreting samples.
changes.commit: No latency sample is a durability or quorum commit.
changes.ack: Report sampled distribution separately from business acknowledgements.
changes.replay_source: Keep raw samples with the run configuration for review.
changes.failure_domain: A local numerical check says nothing about host or network loss.
